coverage.landlord_size_condition: Any local regulation under the exception may not apply to units owned by a person or entity owning fewer than ten rental units.
coverage.summary: Bars rent control in every Massachusetts city and town. The only exception is a voluntary, compensated regulation in a municipality that accepts c. 40P, and that regulation may not apply to units of owners holding fewer than ten rental units or to units with a fair market rent above $400.
coverage.owner_conditions: Exception regulation cannot reach owners of fewer than ten rental units. Six months after initial adoption, owner compliance is entirely voluntary, and the property of an owner who declines is wholly unaffected.
coverage.other_conditions: The exception is available only to a city or town that accepts c. 40P. Even then, the regulation may not apply to units with a fair market rent exceeding $400.

result.notes: Set requires_unknown_facts to false: the statewide ban applies to all municipalities and all residential rentals. Removed from other_conditions the limits on regulating occupancy, services, evictions, condominium conversion and removal from regulation. Those limit what a municipal regulation may contain, not which buildings, units or owners are covered. Added the voluntary owner opt-out after six months to owner_conditions. Listed the owner-portfolio size, the $400 fair market rent limit and the owner opt-out as unverifiable exemptions, because assessor data cannot reliably establish total rental units owned, fair market rent, or opt-out status. The $400 limit is kept in other_conditions and the owner-portfolio limit in landlord_size_condition and owner_conditions, so each appears in both places. These exemptions limit only the narrow exception for municipalities that accept c. 40P; the core rule is a statewide ban. The documents do not show that any municipality has accepted c. 40P.
